methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective dosimetric planning study comparing three SRS techniques (Gamma Knife reference, LINAC single-isocenter, LINAC dual-isocenter) across 28 patients with 197 lesions. Zero-margin strategy applied uniformly across techniques enabling fair comparison. Paddick Conformity Index and low-dose volume metrics (V12, V10, V5, V4, V3) appropriately selected. Paired non-parametric tests and multivariable models used; target coverage requirement (≥99% GTV) standardized. Study design rigorous for dosimetric comparison.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Dosimetric comparison study addressing clinical question: can dual-isocenter LINAC SRS approximate Gamma Knife performance for multiple brain metastases? Findings support clinical implementation of dual-isocenter planning but lack prospective outcome data (survival, toxicity, recurrence) to confirm dosimetric advantages translate to clinical benefit.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods description including patient selection criteria, dose prescription, plan evaluation metrics, and software specifications. Dosimetric analysis transparently reported with paired statistical comparisons. However, lacks pre-registration or protocol publication; patient-level data not available for external validation. Conformity methodology clearly described enabling reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: Demonstrates dual-isocenter LINAC SRS (automated clustering) achieves conformity and dose sparing approaching Gamma Knife, extending prior work showing dual-isocenter benefits. However, multi-isocenter SRS approaches previously reported; current study represents validation/refinement of existing concept using automated planning rather than novel technique development.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear introduction contextualizing clinical challenge (island blocking limits single-isocenter performance). Methods systematically presented with transparent dosimetric parameters and planning algorithms. Results effectively displayed with comparison tables and conformity/low-dose metrics. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings relative to clinical workflow implications.

key_strengths: Large dosimetric comparison study (28 patients, 197 lesions) across three SRS techniques with fair zero-margin comparison assumptions
Demonstrates dual-isocenter planning significantly improves conformity (PCI 0.77 vs 0.73 single-isocenter) and reduces low-dose spread vs single-isocenter
Comprehensive dosimetric metrics (conformity, V3-V12 volumes) appropriate for quality assessment; multivariable analysis identifies predictive factors (target volume, lesion count)
Clinically practical approach using automated planning (Elements MBM) enabling scalability without manual isocenter placement
key_concerns: Retrospective planning study lacking prospective clinical outcome validation; dosimetric improvements not confirmed to translate to reduced toxicity, improved local control, or survival
Comparison with Gamma Knife retrospective with both LINAC techniques; unknown whether GK plans optimized similarly to LINAC planning
No assessment of treatment efficiency (monitor units, delivery time, complexity) despite dual-isocenter requiring additional setup/planning time
Limited to dual-isocenter strategy; three+ isocenter approaches not explored despite potential further conformity improvements
Zero-margin assumption may not reflect real-world practice; margin-related conformity impact not addressed
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality dosimetric planning study demonstrating dual-isocenter LINAC SRS approaches Gamma Knife performance while maintaining clinical feasibility. Appropriate for Tier 3 journals; minor revisions should address clinical outcome validation and treatment efficiency comparisons before clinical implementation recommendations.
